key_insight: In internal evaluation, dLI-RADS achieved 80% lesion-level accuracy versus 74% for LI-RADS, meeting the study’s non-inferiority criterion.
clinical_relevance: The method could support more consistent assessment of small liver lesions on multiphase CT, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Analyzes manually segmented liver lesions on multiphase CT.
Combines neural network predictions with handcrafted measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features.
Uses logistic regression to estimate hepatocellular carcinoma probability.
evidence_signal: This multicenter retrospective study excluded lesions larger than 40 mm and tested internal accuracy non-inferiority using 10,000 bootstrap repetitions with a 5% margin (p = 0.04).
watch_item: The supplied abstract does not report external sensitivity results, leaving generalizability uncertain.
paper_title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
